Project PyrrhusKillzone 2: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)

A native Windows x64 port of the 2009 PS3 game, made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C ahead of time and compiled into a PC program; graphics go through Direct3D 12. No emulator runs at play time.

Status: Partly playable

You need your own copy of the game. This project ships no game code, data, assets or keys.

See the statusSource on GitHub

v0.1.3

29 Oct 2026 · pre-release

  • ChangedA new install starts in a borderless window: the installer, the first-run prompt, the launcher and the game itself all default to it when no display setting exists yet; Alt+Enter switches to a window and back. An existing display.ini keeps its mode, and exclusive fullscreen stays opt-in.
  • ChangedA frame waiting on a graphics job from the game's SPU code is resumed as soon as the job writes its result, instead of after a fixed 4 ms sleep. In two scripted pairs under Proton the wait between the game's frame request and the renderer's drain fell by 4 to 5 ms (median), and the whole time from a button press to the frame being handed to Windows fell by 2 ms in one pair and 12 ms in the other, to about 60 ms; the screen's own delay comes on top and was not measured. Hand play is not measured.
  • ChangedThe release notes on GitHub list each change as its own bullet, with the fixes in a list of their own, instead of one long paragraph.
  • FixedMoving or renaming the unpacked portable folder after (or during) the first run no longer breaks it: CMake's build files kept the old folder's paths, so the build stopped with "CMakeCache.txt directory ... is different" or wrote into a folder with the old name. The first run and the launcher now notice the move, follow saved paths that were inside the folder (an extracted ISO), start the compiler's configure in an empty build folder and keep the lifted code, so only the compile runs again, and only when the game is updated or the build was not finished. A finished game keeps starting as it is. Checked with tests that move a temporary install between runs, not yet with a real portable install on Windows.
  • FixedThe intro movie and the cutscenes were black and silent in every v0.1.2 install: the first run built the game without its movie decoder, because the release did not ship FFmpeg's headers and the build did not ask for them, so the game never loaded the FFmpeg DLLs installed beside it. The release now ships the headers (ffmpeg/include, from the same LGPL FFmpeg build as the DLLs), the first run passes them to the build, the build stops if they are missing, and the first run's last check fails if the game was built without movie decoding. Installing this version over v0.1.2 rebuilds the game once. Reported by @kolomeets80 (#16).
  • FixedThe setup and the first run refuse an install or build folder whose path contains [, ] or ;, with a message, instead of failing later in the build: the bundled CMake cannot work from such a folder. The same failure was reported on Project Helghast (#20).
  • FixedOn a laptop with two graphics chips (for example an Intel iGPU and an NVIDIA or AMD GPU) the game could draw on the weaker chip. It now picks the high-performance adapter first, falls back to the default adapter and then to the software renderer, and writes every adapter it found and which one it chose to the log. Not yet confirmed on a hybrid laptop. Reported by @feanor-noldorin (#13).
  • FixedSwitching to exclusive fullscreen no longer leaves the picture frozen if the next present fails: the swap chain is resized after every switch, a failed present is recovered from (the game leaves fullscreen and keeps drawing in a borderless window; only a lost graphics device, or eight failures in a row, stops the picture). Only tried under Proton, not yet on real Windows.
  • FixedThe first-run log no longer keeps the Windows user name when a path is written in its escaped form, with doubled backslashes (an error message, or a list or JSON of paths). Reported by @feanor-noldorin (#9).
  • Fixedbump_version.py keeps each file's line endings instead of writing Windows line endings when run on Windows. Reported by @feanor-noldorin (#9).

v0.1.2

28 Oct 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedA decrypted disc image (.iso) can be picked instead of a dump folder ("Browse for ISO file" in the setup, or the path in the console). The first run checks the disc inside it, then copies its game files (about 7 GB) into the install folder once; the ISO itself is only read. An encrypted ISO is refused with "this ISO is encrypted; use a decrypted dump".
  • AddedThe setup reads the disc's title id and shows what it found under the folder ("Found: BCUS98116 (Killzone 2, US disc)"). Another game is refused by its title id and name. The Killzone Trilogy disc, whose Killzone 2 is the same title id, is named and allowed as untested.
  • AddedThe game window shows the project's icon in its title bar and taskbar.
  • ChangedPicking the PS3_GAME or PS3_GAME/USRDIR folder of the dump, or the USRDIR folder of the update, works: the setup and the first run use the folder above.
  • ChangedWhen the first start asks for the decrypted EBOOT, a folder is accepted too: it looks for EBOOT.elf in it and in its USRDIR folder, and says where it looked when it is not there. The setup's EBOOT page does the same.
  • ChangedThe update must carry the same title id as the disc; the setup and the first-run check say so when it does not.
  • FixedThe folder hints of the setup and the first-run check offer only Killzone 2 dumps (other games' dumps on a drive are not named) and name up to three .iso files in the folder (or one level down on a drive) beside the folder hints. When no more input comes (a closed console), the first-run check stops with its FAIL lines instead of asking again. The same fixes as Project Helghast PR #17.
  • FixedInstalling into a OneDrive folder is refused, as a precaution taken from a problem reported on Project Helghast: OneDrive synced the build's thousands of files while they were written and locked them. The first-run check also stops when the install or build folder is inside OneDrive (O1), or when a game file is only online in OneDrive (O2, before anything is read, so nothing is downloaded); right-click the game folders and choose "Always keep on this device".
  • FixedWhen the first-run console window is closed with its X, the launcher says so ("its window was closed before it finished; finished steps are kept") instead of showing an error code. It names the first-run log only when the log exists.
  • FixedWhen the setup or the first run stops, the setup's message box, the launcher's dialog and the portable zip's console say why (the same reason the log has). The next start checks your files first and asks again only for the one that was wrong. The setup's EBOOT page refuses the disc's 1.01 EBOOT and names the update's USRDIR folder, where the 1.29 one is; a silent install with /EBOOT= stops with the same text. Adapted from Project Helghast's fix for the same mix-up (its PR #11).
  • FixedWhen a check of your game files fails, the setup's message box, the launcher's dialog and the console say which input failed ("Disc dump", "1.29 update" or "EBOOT"), the path, what is there and what it must hold, and which inputs passed. A disc dump and an update given the wrong way round are named as such, a drive picked instead of a folder gets a pointer to the folders on it that look like the disc or the update, and the disc's PS3_GAME folder given as the update fails its check. Adapted from Project Helghast's fix for the same mix-ups (its PR #14).
  • FixedThe setup's disc page says what a folder without PS3_GAME holds and where PS3_GAME is when it is one folder down; the update page names the path and the missing files, or says the folder is a disc dump.
  • FixedWith a decrypted ISO as the disc, the first-run check could not load its ISO reader under the bundled Python, which does not look in the check's own folder; it now does.
  • FixedGetting your files ready lists what each input must contain, says that the update does not hold the disc archive, and warns against picking a drive instead of the dump folder or the .iso file.
  • FixedUninstalling removes the whole install folder: the first-run logs and their earlier copies no longer keep it behind.
  • Fixed"Verify and rebuild" counts only the files it checked.
  • FixedThe game window's messages (input and window events) are now handled on every frame tick, the same fix as Project Helghast 0.1.4. In our tests a 3.7-second stretch with no messages handled, during a busy catch-up, is gone.
  • FixedThe game's disk cache is rebuilt once when the installed build changes, so the first start after an update loads a little slower. This is a precaution taken from Project Helghast 0.1.4, where a cache left by an older build ended a level with error 20000; it has not been seen on Killzone 2.
  • FixedFiles the game opens to create or append to are now opened the way the console does (the toolkit read three of the open flags with the wrong values). In our tests no visible change yet: the opens seen at start are read-only.
  • FixedThe game window keeps responding while the game builds its graphics pipelines on the first start of a level, which can take several seconds with an empty shader cache: the window now has its own thread, so Windows no longer marks it as not responding. In our tests the longest stretch without an answer went from 7.9 s to 0.05 s; the first start of a level is still slower than later ones.

About the port

how it works

The port is built on ps3recomp (MIT): the PPU code and the game's SPU programs are lifted to C, the PS3 system libraries the game calls are reimplemented, and the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Direct3D 12. The game's archive is read in place from your dump. It is tested on Windows x64 under Proton.

It follows Project Helghast, the same method applied to Killzone 3, and reuses its general runtime work. More in the README.

Full status

Install

v0.1.3 pre-release

29 Oct 2026 · partly playable · Windows x64

Download v0.1.3All releases

The release page has the installer (recommended) and the portable zip, each with a .sha256 file, and SHA256SUMS: check your download against them.

The installer and the portable zip check your own disc dump, the 1.29 update and the decrypted EBOOT, then translate and build the game's code on your machine with a bundled compiler, with one progress bar and a full install log. Nothing of the game is shipped or downloaded; your dump is read where it is, never copied. What each input must contain: Getting your files ready.

Or build the port from source: building.

What goes online

Nothing unless you ask. The port starts no connection of its own; the version check and update download are off until you turn them on. Online multiplayer, if it comes, will only use a self-hosted server you choose. See the README.

Viewing this website loads the Rajdhani font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit; the repository, installer and game do not.

Requirements

What you need

ItemRequiredDetails
Operating systemyesWindows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Tested so far only under Proton on Linux.
Graphics cardyesA GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
Killzone 2 disc dumpyesYour own copy of the US disc (BCUS98116), dumped to a folder or a decrypted ISO file (an encrypted ISO is refused); a FAT32 dump with the disc archive in parts is accepted as it is. Other title ids are refused, naming the id found; the Killzone Trilogy disc (its Killzone 2 is BCUS98116, disc version 02.00) is accepted as untested (what each input must contain).
Update 1.29yesThe game's last update, from your own console or copy.
Decrypted EBOOTyesThe game's main program (EBOOT.elf), decrypted, made from your own copy. This project ships no decryption tools or instructions.

Notice and creditsLicence (MIT)Project Helghast

Killzone and Killzone 2 are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games; the names are used only to say which game the port runs. No game content is distributed: no disc files, no decrypted or translated game code, no assets and no keys. Players supply their own copy of the game; the game's code is translated and compiled on the player's own machine from their own files.

The port's own code, tools and documentation are MIT. Third-party components and credits: NOTICE.md.
